subject: french
title: Stretch: Connectives, Time Phrases & Opinions
welcome_lead: Make your French sound mature with connectives, time phrases and opinion boosters.
meta_desc: GCSE French stretch: connectives, time phrases and opinion phrases for top marks.
final_note: Top marks come from these little extras — sprinkle them through every answer!

walkthroughs.body_html: Examiners love connectives. Try: et (and), mais (but), parce que (because), donc (so), aussi (also), cependant (however), par contre (on the other hand). Example: J'aime le sport, mais je n'aime pas le rugby parce que c'est dangereux.

Time phrases tell the examiner which tense you're using.

  • Past: hier (yesterday), le week-end dernier (last weekend), l'année dernière.
  • Present: d'habitude, normalement, tous les jours.
  • Future: demain, la semaine prochaine, l'année prochaine.
Move beyond j'aime. Try à mon avis (in my opinion), je pense que (I think that), je trouve que (I find that), selon moi (according to me). Add an adjective: À mon avis, le français est passionnant.

mcqs.q: Which time phrase signals the FUTURE tense?
